data.outcome_summary: This OECD working paper uses PISA 2022 to examine how students and teachers use digital resources for learning, combining descriptions of school digital infrastructure with analyses of factors associated with more intensive use. It leverages previously unexamined PISA Teacher Questionnaire data to characterize teachers’ digital-tool use and instructional activities, and it applies cluster analysis to identify distinct patterns in students’, teachers’, and schools’ approaches to digital learning. The paper reports cross-country heterogeneity and highlights that access and quality of digital infrastructure remain barriers in some contexts, even where general provision is near-universal. For teacher outcomes, it reports an index of teacher use of ICT (TCDIGRES) and related patterns by subject taught and by time allocation to instructional activities. The excerpt does not provide model performance metrics typical of predictive ML, and it does not document PV or missing-data handling procedures for the clustering inputs, so results should be interpreted as pattern-based evidence for policy design rather than as causal or predictive performance claims.
